note: Ranks PROBLEMS, not features. score = severity * frequency * observability, each rated 1-5 (max 125). observability = how well GitHub metadata alone can evidence the problem early.

problems.problem: Overlapping in-flight work is discovered at merge time instead of at start time
problems.evidence: external: agent-PR conflict-rate studies; practitioner hotspot-collision reports
problems.existing_coverage: IDE-local tools (GitKraken, GitLive) for your own branch vs target; nothing project-wide or agent-readable

problems.problem: Open loops (stale PRs, branches without a PR, work waiting on other work) accumulate without anyone owning them
problems.evidence: well-known OSS maintenance burden; fully deterministic to detect
problems.existing_coverage: stale bots (close, not surface); PR lists per repo

problems.problem: Nobody has a zero-maintenance picture of which project areas are moving right now
problems.evidence: boards need manual updates; Pulse is per person, not per area

problems.problem: Coding agents start work with no awareness of other in-flight work
problems.evidence: cross-agent conflict rates reported as roughly 2x intra-agent; worktree isolation hides collisions until merge
problems.existing_coverage: orchestrators see only their own sessions; the GitHub MCP gives raw data, not relations

problems.problem: Machine-generated commit bursts drown human-readable signal
The project's trajectory ('how did we get here') cannot be reconstructed
Decisions made in private LLM conversations never reach the shared record
problems.evidence: plausible; mostly unobservable without explicit input
authorship is not ownership; inferring ownership risks surveillance

deprioritised_as_anti_goal.problem: Managers cannot compare individual developer output
deprioritised_as_anti_goal.reason: Serving this need causes surveillance and gaming (R1, R2). Explicitly out of scope.
